page: Hetzner Cloud cpx51 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model under QEMU virtualization. The system is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 360 GB NVMe SSD. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a clear performance profile. The instance exhibits poor single-core CPU performance, placing in the bottom 10% in stress-ng single-core tests. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached operations remains in the average tier, with uncached read speeds reaching 86.13 GB/sec and write speeds at 53.91 GB/sec. Text processing is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% on Geekbench, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput consistently achieve average marks.

The shared CPU allocation model presents a performance tradeoff, as resource contention may affect workloads requiring sustained, predictable single-core execution. Qualitatively, the cpx51 offers a cost-effective resource density for multi-threaded applications that can tolerate shared CPU limits, providing a high core count and local NVMe storage without the premium of dedicated hardware. This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as parallel software compilation, medium-scale web serving, Redis caching layers, and moderate database operations.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between poor single-core CPU execution and average multi-core scaling, with Geekbench and Passmark scores landing in the middle tier. Memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput also perform at average levels. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, making it less suitable for sustained single-threaded tasks. However, the high core density and local NVMe storage offer qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads. The cpx51 is best suited for parallel software compilation, multi-threaded web serving, Redis caching, and moderate database operations.
